intro.en: A compiler translates a program written in a high-level language into machine code. It does this in a pipeline of phases, each with one clear job.
intro.ru: Compiler high-level zubaan mein likhe program ko machine code mein tarjuma karta hai. Yeh kaam phases ki ek pipeline mein hota hai, har phase ka ek wazeh kaam hota hai.

definition.en: The phases of a compiler are lexical analysis, syntax analysis, semantic analysis, intermediate code generation, code optimization and target code generation, supported throughout by the symbol table and the error handler. The first three form the analysis (front end) and the rest the synthesis (back end).
definition.ru: Compiler ke phases yeh hain: lexical analysis, syntax analysis, semantic analysis, intermediate code generation, code optimization aur target code generation; poore amal mein symbol table aur error handler madad karte hain. Pehle teen analysis (front end) aur baqi synthesis (back end) kehlate hain.

explanation.en: Lexical analysis (the scanner) reads characters and groups them into tokens such as identifiers, keywords, numbers and operators, removing spaces and comments. Syntax analysis (the parser) checks that the token sequence follows the grammar and builds a parse tree or abstract syntax tree. Semantic analysis checks meaning: declared variables, matching types, correct number of arguments. Intermediate code generation produces a machine-independent form such as three-address code. Code optimization improves it (constant folding, removing dead code, common sub-expressions). Code generation maps it to the target machine's instructions and registers. The symbol table stores information about identifiers (name, type, scope) for all phases. An interpreter executes the program directly instead of producing a separate machine-code file.
explanation.ru: Lexical analysis (scanner) characters parh kar unhein tokens mein jorta hai jaise identifiers, keywords, numbers aur operators, aur spaces aur comments hata deta hai. Syntax analysis (parser) check karta hai ke tokens ki tarteeb grammar ke mutabiq hai aur parse tree ya abstract syntax tree banata hai. Semantic analysis maani check karta hai: variables declare hue, types milti hain, arguments ki sahi tadaad. Intermediate code generation machine se azad shakal banati hai jaise three-address code. Code optimization use behtar karti hai (constant folding, dead code hatana, common sub-expressions). Code generation use target machine ki instructions aur registers par map karti hai. Symbol table har phase ke liye identifiers ki maloomat (naam, type, scope) rakhti hai. Interpreter alag machine-code file banaye baghair program seedha chalata hai.

example.en: Statement: position = initial + rate * 60. Lexer: id(position) = id(initial) + id(rate) * num(60). Parser: tree with = at the root and * below +. Semantic: 60 is converted to a float because rate is float. Intermediate code: t1 = rate * 60.0; t2 = initial + t1; position = t2. Optimizer: t1 = rate * 60.0; position = initial + t1. Code generator: MUL R2, 60.0 ... STORE position.
example.ru: Statement: position = initial + rate * 60. Lexer: id(position) = id(initial) + id(rate) * num(60). Parser: tree jis ki root par = aur + ke neeche * hai. Semantic: rate float hai is liye 60 float mein badla jata hai. Intermediate code: t1 = rate * 60.0; t2 = initial + t1; position = t2. Optimizer: t1 = rate * 60.0; position = initial + t1. Code generator: MUL R2, 60.0 ... STORE position.

intro.en: Before a compiler can understand a program it must split the stream of characters into words. That is the job of the lexical analyser, which is built from regular expressions and finite automata.
intro.ru: Program samajhne se pehle compiler ko characters ki dhaar ko alfaaz mein todna hota hai. Yeh lexical analyser ka kaam hai, jo regular expressions aur finite automata se banta hai.

definition.en: Lexical analysis converts the source text into a sequence of tokens. Each token class (identifier, number, keyword, operator) is described by a regular expression, and the scanner recognises them with a deterministic finite automaton (DFA).
definition.ru: Lexical analysis source text ko tokens ki tarteeb mein badalta hai. Har token class (identifier, number, keyword, operator) ek regular expression se bayan hoti hai, aur scanner unhein deterministic finite automaton (DFA) se pehchanta hai.

explanation.en: A lexeme is the actual text (for example 'count'), the token is its class (IDENTIFIER) and the pattern is the rule that describes the class (letter followed by letters or digits). Regular expressions combine characters with union (a|b), concatenation (ab) and Kleene star (a*). Thompson's construction turns a regular expression into an NFA; subset construction turns the NFA into a DFA, which reads each character once and is very fast. When several patterns match, the scanner uses the longest match ('<=' rather than '<') and, for equal length, the rule listed first (keywords before identifiers). The lexer also skips whitespace and comments, records line numbers for error messages and enters identifiers into the symbol table.
explanation.ru: Lexeme asal text hai (maslan 'count'), token us ki class hai (IDENTIFIER) aur pattern woh qaida hai jo class bayan karta hai (letter ke baad letters ya digits). Regular expressions characters ko union (a|b), concatenation (ab) aur Kleene star (a*) se jorti hain. Thompson's construction regular expression ko NFA banati hai; subset construction NFA ko DFA mein badalti hai, jo har character ek dafa parhta hai aur bohat tez hai. Jab kai patterns milein to scanner sab se lamba match leta hai ('<' ki jagah '<=') aur barabar length par pehle likha qaida (keywords identifiers se pehle). Lexer whitespace aur comments chhor deta hai, error messages ke liye line numbers yaad rakhta hai aur identifiers ko symbol table mein dalta hai.

example.en: Input: if (count <= 10) total = total + 1; Tokens: KEYWORD(if), LPAREN, ID(count), RELOP(<=), NUM(10), RPAREN, ID(total), ASSIGN, ID(total), PLUS, NUM(1), SEMICOLON - 12 tokens. Try it in the lexer simulator.

intro.en: A programming language's syntax is defined by a grammar. The parser uses it to check programs and to build the tree that the rest of the compiler works on.
intro.ru: Programming language ka syntax grammar se tay hota hai. Parser isi se programs check karta hai aur woh tree banata hai jis par baqi compiler kaam karta hai.

definition.en: A context-free grammar (CFG) has terminals (tokens), non-terminals (syntactic categories), a start symbol and productions of the form A -> alpha. A derivation repeatedly replaces a non-terminal by the right side of one of its productions; a parse tree shows a derivation as a tree.
definition.ru: Context-free grammar (CFG) mein terminals (tokens), non-terminals (syntax ki categories), ek start symbol aur A -> alpha jaisi productions hoti hain. Derivation baar baar non-terminal ko us ki kisi production ke right side se badalti hai; parse tree derivation ko tree ki shakal mein dikhata hai.

explanation.en: In a leftmost derivation the leftmost non-terminal is replaced at each step (top-down parsers produce this); in a rightmost derivation the rightmost one is (bottom-up parsers produce its reverse). A grammar is ambiguous if some string has two different parse trees, for example E -> E + E | E * E | id for 'id + id * id'. Ambiguity is removed by rewriting the grammar with one non-terminal per precedence level: E -> E + T | T, T -> T * F | F, F -> ( E ) | id, which makes * bind tighter than + and both left-associative. Top-down (LL) parsers cannot handle left recursion such as E -> E + T, so it is rewritten as E -> T E', E' -> + T E' | epsilon; common prefixes are removed by left factoring.
explanation.ru: Leftmost derivation mein har step par sab se baayan non-terminal badla jata hai (top-down parsers yahi banate hain); rightmost derivation mein sab se daayan (bottom-up parsers is ka ulat banate hain). Grammar ambiguous hai agar kisi string ke do mukhtalif parse trees hon, maslan 'id + id * id' ke liye E -> E + E | E * E | id. Ambiguity har precedence level ke liye alag non-terminal bana kar khatam hoti hai: E -> E + T | T, T -> T * F | F, F -> ( E ) | id, jis se * ki pakar + se mazboot aur dono left-associative ho jate hain. Top-down (LL) parsers E -> E + T jaisi left recursion nahi sambhal sakte, is liye ise E -> T E', E' -> + T E' | epsilon likha jata hai; mushtarik prefixes left factoring se hatate hain.

example.en: Grammar E -> E + T | T, T -> T * F | F, F -> id. Leftmost derivation of id + id * id: E => E + T => T + T => F + T => id + T => id + T * F => id + F * F => id + id * F => id + id * id. In the parse tree the * node sits below the + node, so multiplication happens first.
example.ru: Grammar E -> E + T | T, T -> T * F | F, F -> id. id + id * id ki leftmost derivation: E => E + T => T + T => F + T => id + T => id + T * F => id + F * F => id + id * F => id + id * id. Parse tree mein * wala node + wale node ke neeche hai, is liye zarab pehle hoti hai.

intro.en: An LL(1) parser reads input left to right and decides each step by looking at just one token. It is built from two sets computed from the grammar: FIRST and FOLLOW.
intro.ru: LL(1) parser input baayen se daayen parhta hai aur har step sirf ek token dekh kar tay karta hai. Yeh grammar se nikalne wale do sets se banta hai: FIRST aur FOLLOW.

definition.en: FIRST(alpha) is the set of terminals that can begin strings derived from alpha (plus epsilon if alpha can derive the empty string). FOLLOW(A) is the set of terminals that can appear immediately after A in some sentential form ($ for the end). A grammar is LL(1) if its predictive parsing table built from these sets has at most one production in every cell.
definition.ru: FIRST(alpha) un terminals ka set hai jin se alpha se banne wali strings shuru ho sakti hain (aur epsilon agar alpha khali string bana sake). FOLLOW(A) un terminals ka set hai jo kisi sentential form mein A ke foran baad aa sakte hain (aakhir ke liye $). Grammar LL(1) hai agar in sets se bani predictive parsing table ke har khane mein zyada se zyada ek production ho.

explanation.en: FIRST rules: for a terminal a, FIRST(a) = {a}; for A -> X1 X2 ..., add FIRST(X1) without epsilon, and if X1 can be empty continue with X2, and so on. FOLLOW rules: put $ in FOLLOW(start); for A -> alpha B beta add FIRST(beta) without epsilon to FOLLOW(B); if beta can be empty (or is missing) add FOLLOW(A) to FOLLOW(B). Table: for each production A -> alpha, put it in M[A, a] for every a in FIRST(alpha); if epsilon is in FIRST(alpha), also for every b in FOLLOW(A). The parser keeps a stack starting with $ and the start symbol: if the top is a terminal it must match the input; if it is a non-terminal, the table entry tells which production to expand. An empty or double entry means a syntax error or a non-LL(1) grammar.
explanation.ru: FIRST ke qaide: terminal a ke liye FIRST(a) = {a}; A -> X1 X2 ... ke liye FIRST(X1) (epsilon ke baghair) shamil karein, aur agar X1 khali ho sakta hai to X2 par jayein, waghera. FOLLOW ke qaide: start ke FOLLOW mein $ dalein; A -> alpha B beta ke liye FIRST(beta) (epsilon ke baghair) FOLLOW(B) mein dalein; agar beta khali ho sakta hai (ya maujood hi nahi) to FOLLOW(A) ko FOLLOW(B) mein dalein. Table: har production A -> alpha ko FIRST(alpha) ke har a ke liye M[A, a] mein rakhein; agar FIRST(alpha) mein epsilon ho to FOLLOW(A) ke har b ke liye bhi. Parser ka stack $ aur start symbol se shuru hota hai: upar terminal ho to input se milna chahiye; non-terminal ho to table batati hai kaunsi production phailani hai. Khali ya do entries wala khana syntax error ya non-LL(1) grammar ki nishani hai.

example.en: E -> T E', E' -> + T E' | eps, T -> F T', T' -> * F T' | eps, F -> ( E ) | id. FIRST(E) = FIRST(T) = FIRST(F) = { (, id }; FIRST(E') = { +, eps }; FIRST(T') = { *, eps }. FOLLOW(E) = FOLLOW(E') = { ), $ }; FOLLOW(T) = FOLLOW(T') = { +, ), $ }; FOLLOW(F) = { *, +, ), $ }. Use the FIRST/FOLLOW tool to compute these and parse id + id * id.
example.ru: E -> T E', E' -> + T E' | eps, T -> F T', T' -> * F T' | eps, F -> ( E ) | id. FIRST(E) = FIRST(T) = FIRST(F) = { (, id }; FIRST(E') = { +, eps }; FIRST(T') = { *, eps }. FOLLOW(E) = FOLLOW(E') = { ), $ }; FOLLOW(T) = FOLLOW(T') = { +, ), $ }; FOLLOW(F) = { *, +, ), $ }. Yeh sets nikalne aur id + id * id parse karne ke liye FIRST/FOLLOW tool istemal karein.

intro.en: Bottom-up parsers build the parse tree from the leaves up to the root. LR parsers are the most powerful practical parsers and are generated automatically by tools such as yacc and bison.
intro.ru: Bottom-up parsers parse tree ko patton (leaves) se root ki taraf banate hain. LR parsers sab se taqatwar amli parsers hain aur yacc aur bison jaise tools inhein khud banate hain.

definition.en: A shift-reduce parser uses a stack and four actions: shift (push the next input token), reduce (replace a handle on top of the stack by the left side of a production), accept and error. LR parsers decide these actions with a table built from LR items; SLR, LALR and canonical LR(1) differ in how much lookahead information they use.
definition.ru: Shift-reduce parser stack aur chaar actions istemal karta hai: shift (agla input token stack par dalna), reduce (stack ke upar maujood handle ko production ke left side se badalna), accept aur error. LR parsers yeh actions LR items se bani table se tay karte hain; SLR, LALR aur canonical LR(1) is mein mukhtalif hain ke kitni lookahead maloomat istemal karte hain.

explanation.en: A handle is the substring that matches a production's right side and whose reduction is a step of the rightmost derivation in reverse. An LR(0) item is a production with a dot showing how much has been seen, e.g. E -> E . + T. The closure and goto operations build a DFA of item sets (the canonical collection); its states become the rows of the ACTION and GOTO tables. SLR puts a reduce in the columns of FOLLOW of the left side; LALR and LR(1) use more precise lookaheads and accept more grammars. A shift-reduce conflict happens when both actions are possible in a cell (the dangling else); a reduce-reduce conflict when two reductions are possible. LR parsers handle left recursion naturally and detect errors as early as possible.
explanation.ru: Handle woh substring hai jo kisi production ke right side se milta hai aur jis ka reduction rightmost derivation ka ulta qadam hai. LR(0) item dot wali production hai jo batati hai kitna dekha ja chuka hai, maslan E -> E . + T. Closure aur goto operations item sets ka DFA (canonical collection) banate hain; is ki states ACTION aur GOTO tables ki rows banti hain. SLR reduce ko left side ke FOLLOW wale columns mein rakhta hai; LALR aur LR(1) zyada durust lookaheads istemal karte hain aur zyada grammars qubool karte hain. Shift-reduce conflict tab hota hai jab ek khane mein dono actions mumkin hon (dangling else); reduce-reduce conflict jab do reductions mumkin hon. LR parsers left recursion qudrati tor par sambhalte hain aur errors jald se jald pakarte hain.

example.en: Grammar E -> E + id | id, input id + id. Stack $ / input id + id $: shift id; reduce E -> id (stack $ E); shift +; shift id (stack $ E + id); reduce E -> E + id (stack $ E); accept. The shift-reduce simulator shows each step.

intro.en: Between the parse tree and machine code, compilers use a simple intermediate language. It is easy to generate, easy to optimise and independent of the target machine.
intro.ru: Parse tree aur machine code ke darmiyan compilers ek saada intermediate zubaan istemal karte hain. Ise banana aur optimise karna aasan hai aur yeh target machine se azad hai.

definition.en: Three-address code (TAC) is an intermediate representation in which each instruction has at most one operator and at most three addresses, for example t1 = b * c. Code optimization transforms the code to run faster or use less memory without changing its meaning.
definition.ru: Three-address code (TAC) aisi intermediate representation hai jis ki har instruction mein zyada se zyada ek operator aur teen addresses hote hain, maslan t1 = b * c. Code optimization code ko maani badle baghair tez chalne ya kam memory lene wala banati hai.

explanation.en: TAC is produced by walking the syntax tree: each operator node gets a new temporary that holds its result. Common forms are assignments, copies, conditional and unconditional jumps (if x < y goto L1), and procedure calls. TAC is stored as quadruples (op, arg1, arg2, result) or triples (results referred to by position). The code is split into basic blocks - straight-line sequences with one entry and one exit - which form a control-flow graph. Typical optimizations: constant folding (2 * 3 becomes 6), constant propagation, common sub-expression elimination (compute b * c once), dead-code elimination (remove results never used), copy propagation, and loop optimizations such as moving loop-invariant code out of the loop and strength reduction (replace i * 4 by repeated addition).
explanation.ru: TAC syntax tree par chal kar banta hai: har operator node ko naya temporary milta hai jo us ka natija rakhta hai. Aam shaklein assignments, copies, conditional aur unconditional jumps (if x < y goto L1), aur procedure calls hain. TAC quadruples (op, arg1, arg2, result) ya triples (natije position se) ki shakal mein rakha jata hai. Code basic blocks mein toot-ta hai - seedhe silsile jin ka ek darwaza andar aur ek bahar - jo control-flow graph banate hain. Aam optimizations: constant folding (2 * 3 ban jata hai 6), constant propagation, common sub-expression elimination (b * c ek dafa nikalna), dead-code elimination (kabhi istemal na hone wale natije hatana), copy propagation, aur loop optimizations jaise loop-invariant code ko loop se bahar nikalna aur strength reduction (i * 4 ko baar baar jama se badalna).

example.en: a = b * c + b * c - 2 * 3. TAC: t1 = b * c; t2 = b * c; t3 = t1 + t2; t4 = 2 * 3; t5 = t3 - t4; a = t5. After common sub-expression elimination and constant folding: t1 = b * c; t3 = t1 + t1; a = t3 - 6.
example.ru: a = b * c + b * c - 2 * 3. TAC: t1 = b * c; t2 = b * c; t3 = t1 + t2; t4 = 2 * 3; t5 = t3 - t4; a = t5. Common sub-expression elimination aur constant folding ke baad: t1 = b * c; t3 = t1 + t1; a = t3 - 6.
